not a part: A fragment: 'petiole' and 'leaves' run together by the parser; the statements belong to petiole (PO_0020038) or leaf.

not a part: A quality suffix ('5-8-ribbed'), already handled by config/flora_counted_parts.tsv (ribbed -> rib count on the organ described). Like 'winged' in the previous review, it is not a plant structure.
not a part: A fragment: 'inflorescence' cut off by the tokenizer. The values (spiciform, paniculiform, corymbiform) belong to inflorescence (PO_0009049); fix the split rather than add a rule.

Stipule-like structures of different origins (prophylls of axillary buds in Bignoniaceae, basal leaflets in Fabaceae and Sapindaceae, petiole outgrowths). They are not stipules (PO_0020041), and no single class or parent fits all uses. Too few statements (25) to justify a heterogeneous new class.

not a part: A quality (orientation), not a structure. The examples are 'spreading pinnae', 'spreading branches' and 'spreading rootstock': the bearer is the noun that follows and 'spreading' is its quality.

not a part: A fragment: 'inflorescence' cut and run together with another token. The statements (axis pilose, spike flexuous, ebracteate) belong to inflorescence (PO_0009049). Fix the tokenizer, as for 'inflores'.
not a part: A fragment of 'inflorescence' (and 'inflorescences', French 'inflorescence') cut by the tokenizer. The values (dense, lax, showy, Heads, Panicules) belong to inflorescence (PO_0009049).

not a part: A quality. The examples are the noun 'mucro' ('tipped by a mucro 1-2 mm long'), which has no PO class; 'with a mucro' should be read as the organ described + mucronate (FLOPO_0991054). The length of the mucro is a length of the organ's apex.

not a part: A fragment: the bearer 'gland' run together with the quality 'present'. The structure is portion of secretory tissue (PO_0005656, synonym gland); leaf and petiole glands near the petiole base are extrafloral nectary (PO_0009057, synonym petiolar gland). Fix the split.

The word means different things in different floras: a cushion-plant habit ('cushions or mats'), a cushion-shaped floral disc ('central yellowish green cushion'), French 'coussinets' (pulvini or leaf cushions), and thickenings of a corona ('5 épaississements'). The shape sense is already handled by cushion-shaped = pulvinate (PATO:0001357).

not a part: A quality, not a part. 'n-branched' is a count of the branches of the part named before it (tendril, style), handled by the count-of-parts pattern 03. Some examples are fragments ('style branches', 'rootstock').

not a part: An adjective. In 'capitate glands' the bearer is the gland (portion of secretory tissue PO_0005656) or a glandular trichome (PO_0004509), and the quality is head-shaped. 'Épis capituliformes' is the inflorescence arrangement.

A generic part that needs the organ it belongs to: spinules on leaf margins (teeth, 'spinulose-serrulate'), on pollen or spores ('narrowly cylindric'), or on stems. This matches the earlier rejections of 'bristle' and 'horn'.
not a part: 'n-cleft' is a count of lobes, already handled by the counted-parts rule. 'Clefts 1.5-3 mm' is the depth of an incision, a quality of the lobed part, not a structure.
A generic part that needs the organ it belongs to (moss leaf, bract, glume, sepal), like 'margin' and 'rim' before. The moss-leaf sense is covered under 'leaf border'.
not a part: A fragment of a count ('5-7 each side'), meaning a count per side of the rachis or midrib. The earlier review rejected 'per side' as not a plant structure.

Generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to. Floras use it for the mouth of the perigynium beak, of the leaf sheath (Carex), of the corolla, and so on. Same reason as the earlier rejections of mouth-like words (throat, opening).

Ambiguous. In FNA it is mostly the involucral fruit husk of Carya and Juglandaceae ('husk winged to base', 'sutures winged'). PO's synonym husk → inflorescence bract (PO_0009054) fits the maize husk, not that one. Other uses refer to any outer fruit covering.
not a part: A density unit ('10-15 lateral veins per cm'), not a structure. Like 'per node' and 'per side' in the earlier review.

not a part: The second term of a length ratio ('1/2-3/4 the length of the calyx'). This is pattern 10, ratio to another part, with calyx PO_0009060 as the reference. Like 'leaf length' and 'times calyx' earlier.

Two unrelated structures share the name. In Acanthaceae it is the hooked funicle (jaculator) that throws the seeds ('long and curved', 'subacute at tip'). In Apocynaceae and orchids it is the corpusculum or viscid gland of the pollinarium ('ellipsoid', 'linear-oblong'). It cannot be grounded without the family.
not a part: A surface marking, not a structure. Its presence and number are the quality striated (PATO_0001410) of the part that bears the striae, which is counted with pattern 3 ('4-5-striate').

not a part: A quality (PATO_0000454 hairy), here produced by a lemmatisation error on the noun hairs/poils. The noun should ground to trichome (PO_0000282), which lists hair as a synonym. A bearer rule on 'hairy' would misfire on its adjectival uses.
not a part: A fragment of relative measurements ('1/3-1/2 as long as spikelet'), handled by pattern 10, ratio to another part.
Generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to (cell wall, ovary wall, fruit wall, capsule wall). Like 'layer' and 'membrane' earlier.
not a part: A colour or surface marking, not a structure: the quality striated (PATO_0001410) or a colour pattern of the part that bears the stripes. Counts go by pattern 3 ('7-16-striate').
not a part: The quality striated (PATO_0001410) of the part that bears the striations. Counts go by pattern 3.
not a part: A count of one ('stems single', 'flowers single'), a value of the amount of the part named next to it.

not a part: A colour marking, not a structure: the quality blotchy (PATO_0000329) of the petal or lip that bears it. Its colour and shape are better recorded as attributes of the marking than as a bearer.
not a part: A comparison of size with no second term ('2 larger ones'), like 'smaller' and 'broader', which were rejected on 2026-11-13.

not a part: A counting suffix, not a part. Note: flora_counted_parts.tsv maps 'celled' to locule, but these examples count the cells of hairs and paraphyses ('1--4-celled distal portion', 'paraphyses 3-8-celled'). There the counted part is plant cell (PO_0009002), not locule.

not a part: Comes from 'jugate' or 'juguées': a count of leaflet pairs. It is already covered by the 'jugate' suffix (leaflet, collection size 2) in flora_counted_parts.tsv. The French '-juguée(s)' form should be added to that suffix. 'jugate' was rejected as not a structure on 2026-11-13.
not a part: A branching quality with a count ('2--3-forked'), not a part.
not a part: Describes the counted veins or lines ('3 parallel veins'). It is an arrangement quality, not a part.
not a part: A colour word describing the counted part ('3 pale veins', 'pale lenticels').

The plural of 'margin', which was rejected on 2026-11-13 as a general part that needs its organ. It should be handled as the region 'margin' of the organ being described (for example leaf lamina margin, PO_0025009), not as a bearer of its own.
not a part: A shape word describing counted teeth, lobes or ridges.
The plural of 'scar', rejected on 2026-11-13 as a general part. 'leaf-scars' should go to leaf scar (FLOPO_0986052). Pedicel scars and hair scars need their organ.
not a part: A position quality of the counted flowers or umbels, not a part.
not a part: An arrangement quality ('leaves 6-8 whorled', 'in 2 whorls of 3'). 'whorl' and 'verticil' were rejected as general parts on 2026-11-13.
not a part: A shape word describing appendages, warts or outgrowths.
not a part: A surface quality ('tuberculate appendages'). The 'tubercles' in these examples are general outgrowths. They are not PO tubercle (PO_0025352), which is the cactus podarium.
not a part: A margin quality of counted lobes (entire, FLOPO_0985009).

A general part that needs its organ (labellum, corolla, leaf or corona). 'mid-lobe', 'midlobe' and 'lateral lobe' were rejected for the same reason on 2026-11-13. When the organ is known it is that organ's lobe in median position (for example labellum lobe, FLOPO_0986028).

not a part: A piece of a count ('setae 1-2 per perichaetium'), like 'per node' and 'per axil', which the previous review rejected. The part being counted is the seta; the perichaetium is only the unit.

not a part: A substance, and a general word covering latex, resin, gum and sap. The specific words already have classes: plant latex (FLOPO_0980431), plant resin (PO_0025603), plant sap (PO_0025538). Ground those words, not 'exudate'.

Two different structures share this name. In mosses it is the swollen capsule base (a synonym of sporangium base, PO_0030040). In Pinus it is the exposed thickened end of the cone scale (rhombic, keeled, pyramidal, recurved, as in the examples). It cannot be grounded without knowing which group the flora covers.
not a part: An adjective meaning 'bearing appendages', not a part. The appendage itself is a general word that needs its organ, and the previous review rejected 'appendaged' the same way.

not a part: A piece of a count from Anthurium spadix descriptions ('4-6 flowers visible in the alternate spiral'). It is a way of counting flowers along a spiral, not a structure; 'spiral' was rejected before.
not a part: A piece of a count from Anthurium spadix descriptions ('7-11 flowers visible in principal spiral'). It is a counting convention, not a structure.
not a part: A piece of a count ('2-3 rows of cells' in a border or lamina, as in Fissidens). The bearer is the border or lamina named nearby, and 'cell' alone was rejected before.

A general part that needs its organ, like 'lateral lobe' in the previous review. 'Primary' gives a level of division that has no value class. It is mostly leaf lobes but also lobes of other organs. The flora's own organ word should carry the bearer, with leaf lamina lobe (PO_0025517) where it is a leaf.
not a part: A quality of the arrangement of flowers, leaves etc., not a structure; 'en touffe', 'in clusters of' likewise. FLOPO:0991098 fascicled also exists for clusters from one point.

Same as 'lateral lobe', rejected on 2026-11-13: generic part, needs the organ it belongs to (labellum, corolla, leaf, rostellum...). Where the organ is named, its lobe class (labellum lobe FLOPO_0986028, corolla lobe FLOPO_0986006, leaf lamina lobe PO_0025517) takes the statement.

An alternative of two generic parts ('2-6 teeth or lobes'), with no organ named; tooth and lobe alone need the organ they belong to. Where the organ is named, count with pattern 03 on its lobe or tooth class.
not a part: A quality of the bearer (having glands), not a structure.
not a part: A ratio phrase ('2-3 times as long as the tube'), not a structure; as 'times calyx' and 'times width' (rejected 2026-11-13).
Generic part (folds), needs the organ it belongs to; 'fold' was rejected on 2026-11-13. '4-6-plicate' is a count of folds of a named organ (pattern 03) or the quality plicate (PATO_0104365).
Generic part, needs the organ it belongs to (here the hyaline cells of Sphagnum leaves); 'pore' was rejected on 2026-11-13.
not a part: A count phrase ('1-3 per leaf axil'), not the part described; 'per axil' and 'per node' were rejected on 2026-11-13.

Ambiguous: in rattans a whip-like sterile inflorescence on the leaf sheath ('to 2 m long, armed with hooks'), in mosses a thin branch ('root-like flagellums'), elsewhere a whip-like tip. A rattan flagellum class may be worth adding later with a palm-only context rule.
not a part: A sex quality with its noun left out ('1 ou 3 fleurs ♀', '56-183 ♀'); already a context word in config/flora_context_words.tsv.
not a part: A sex quality with its noun left out ('bisexual 18-25', 'Bisexual florets ca. 5').
not a part: A count phrase, not a structure; 'per whorl' was rejected on 2026-11-13.

Generic and mixed: fruit hooks ('hooks per keel'), axillary hooks that are modified branches or inflorescences ('crochets axillaires'), prickles. PO's apical hook (PO_0000012) is the seedling hypocotyl hook and does not apply.
not a part: A quality (having a stipe), not a structure; 'with a stipe 2 mm' is a measurement of the stalk.
not a part: A quality of the arrangement ('widely spaced pairs'), not a structure. 'evenly spaced' has no term and stays unmapped.

In floras 'fibres' are mostly the fibrous remains of palm leaf sheaths (up to 80 cm long, black, robust), and sometimes mesocarp or bark fibres. PO plant fiber cell (PO_0025407) is a single sclerenchyma cell and does not fit. Without the organ it belongs to, the word is ambiguous.

A lemmatisation fragment of 'axes'. Secondary or primary axes may be inflorescence branches or stem branches, so the word needs the organ it belongs to. The previous review rejected 'axis' for the same reason.
not a part: A length-to-width ratio ('3-7 × as long as wide'). This is pattern 11, ratio of two dimensions, of the part named in the sentence. It is not a bearer.
French 'pièces' means the members of any whorl (calyx, perianth, involucre, operculum). This is a generic part that needs the organ it belongs to.
A generic surface feature (on seeds, pyrenes, fruits, stems) that needs the organ it belongs to, like 'pit' and 'groove' in the previous review.

not a part: A dimension used as the second term of a ratio ('costa filling 1/2-2/3 of leaf width'). This is pattern 10, ratio to another part: costa width relative to the width of leaf PO_0025034 / non-vascular leaf PO_0025075.
not a part: A position adjective cut off from its noun ('3 pairs of distal leaflets'). It is a series position of the bearer (pattern 04), not a part.
A generic part (on a petal, corona or corolla throat) that needs the organ it belongs to. Where the statement only says the organ is pouched, use the quality saccate (FLOPO:0991140).
A generic outgrowth (of the calyx or another organ) that needs the organ it belongs to, like 'appendage' in the previous review.
not a part: An adverb fragment of 'deeply lobed / dissected'. It belongs to the quality of the following noun.

The end cell of a hair, filament, paraphysis or algal branchlet. It is a generic cell that needs the structure it ends. The previous review rejected 'cell'. Axillary hair terminal cell (PO_0025317) applies only when the text names an axillary hair.
A network of veins on leaves, of ridges on seeds or pollen, or of fibres. It is ambiguous without the organ. Where the organ is given, the quality is reticulate (FLOPO:0991100).
not a part: A quality adjective ('3-tufted', 'tufted domatia'), or 'tuft' meaning a tuft of hairs, which is already covered by coma (PO_0020061) or bearded (FLOPO:0991118). It is not a part.
not a part: A quality (PATO_0001354 translucent). In these phrases it describes pellucid gland dots or cells, which are the real bearer.

It mixes cactus areole spines (spine leaf PO_0025173) with spiny teeth on leaf margins ('margin with 5-13 lateral spines'). 'Lateral' is a position the patterns do not hold. The last review rejected 'lateral lobe' for the same reason.
Generic part that needs the organ it belongs to: Aristolochia perianth flap, fruit flaps, moss peristome or leaf flaps.

These are counts and wall traits of cells in a cross-section, mostly in bryophytes or algae-like descriptions. Pith (PO_0006109, synonym medulla) is the closest class, but which organ is meant is unclear and the counts are anatomy, not a phenotype of the whole pith.

Generic part that needs the organ: fruit furrows, stem grooves, pollen apertures ('3-sulcate'). PO canal (PO_0025132) lists sulci as a synonym, but the last review rejected 'groove' (another canal synonym) as a generic part. Kept the same here.
not a part: An arrangement quality ('flower solitary', 'scape solitary'): the part occurs singly. It is not a part, and the amount reading (count 1) belongs to the part named.
The walls of basal cells of moss leaves or of hairs. A cell wall is a GO cellular component (cell wall, GO:0005618), not a PO structure, and the organ is not given.
Same as 'sulci': a generic groove (canal PO_0025132 synonym) that needs its organ, rejected the same way as 'groove'.
Generic part: the cut or gap between lobes or teeth of whatever organ is being described.
not a part: A size quality of a set of parts (close to FLOPO equal/unequal, FLOPO_0991102/0991101). The counted part is the noun that follows it ('subequal lobes').

not a part: An adjective. 'N-keeled' is handled by the counted-part suffix (keeled -> keel). Caution: PO keel (PO_0025327) is the two lower petals of a pea-type flower. A keel meaning a ridge ('disc with 2 keels', 'à crête médiane') must not ground to PO_0025327.
not a part: A position word that modifies the noun after it (dorsal ridges, grooves, wings, vittae).
not a part: A quality (PATO_0002211 recurved) of the counted teeth, valves or lobules.

A generic space or gap that needs its organ: air spaces beside the midrib of Potamogeton leaves, a gap in a perianth tube. PO lists lacuna as a synonym of plant anatomical space (PO_0025117), which is too general to use alone. Rejected the same way as 'pore' and 'pit'.
Generic: a tooth, tip, awn or cusp of whatever organ is being described ('lobes 1-3-pointed', 'pointes filamenteuses').
Generic part ('lames', 'plates' on a disc, seed or fruit) that needs its organ.
not a part: A division quality: '2-ternate' means compound in threes twice over. The number is the degree of division, not a count of parts.
Generic: a thickened zone of any organ (disc, wall, pericarp) that needs its organ.
not a part: An arrangement quality, nearly opposite. The counted part is the noun that follows it (pairs of leaflets, lobes, costae).

not a part: Scope of a count ('1-5 per leaf'): the leaf is the whole in which the counted parts (sori, involucres) occur, as in 'per node' and 'per side'; pattern 03 count of parts with the leaf as the whole.
not a part: A quality of the counted teeth, ribs or projections: PATO_0001419 sharp.
not a part: A quality word; 'adventitious roots' as a whole should ground to shoot-borne root (PO_0000042, BROAD synonym adventitious root), 'adventitious shoots' to a shoot with that qualifier.
not a part: A quality: PATO_0002311 fimbriated / PATO_0040008 fringed; '2-3-fimbriate' is a count of fimbriae, and 'fimbria' was rejected as a generic part in the previous review.
not a part: An arrangement (rows of hairs, scales, cells), not a structure; it needs the parts it arranges (cf. 'tier', 'line' rejected before).
not a part: Fragment of a ratio ('3-5 x as long as the petiole'): pattern 10 ratio to another part, with petiole (PO_0020038) as the other part.
not a part: Position quality PATO_0002476 terminal, already a bearer_quality in config/flora_context_words.tsv.
not a part: A position qualifier of the grooves, protrusions or rows it precedes, not a structure.
Generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to ('ovary rudiment' = pistillode PO_0009078; grass rudiments are reduced sterile florets).
not a part: A size quality of the following part (teeth, serrations), not a structure.
not a part: A broken word: the examples mix inflorescences, heads and spikelets; fix the normalisation that produced it rather than ground it.
not a part: An order of branching or a height of insertion ('4 levels of branching', 'anthers at 2 levels'), not a structure.
Ambiguous: a fertile cone scale (megasporophyll PO_0009027) in conifers, a fertile glume in Cyperaceae spikelets.
not a part: Degree adverb.
not a part: Count suffix like 'nerved' ('3-nervate'): add 'nervate -> vein' to config/flora_counted_parts.tsv; 'lateral nerves' already grounds by rule C274.
Plural of 'appendage', rejected as a generic part in the previous review: it needs the organ it belongs to.
not a part: A quality of the counted teeth or points (the botanical acute shape), not a structure.
not a part: Shape quality PATO_0001891 ovate of the following part (glands, leaflets).
not a part: A broken word: most examples are the perianth tube (already FLOPO_0986010), one is a resupinate flower; fix the normalisation rather than ground it.
not a part: The unit a count is given per ('spines 30-51 per areole'), not a bearer; same as 'per node' and 'per side' in the previous review. The counted part (spine, sorus) is the bearer.
not a part: '2-3-stratose' gives the number of cell layers of the lamina or margin. It is a quality (count or thickness) of that part, not a part.
Generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to (leaf, lip, corolla), like 'lateral lobe' in the previous review.
not a part: A quality-word fragment of 'pairs of free pinnules/leaflets'. The counted part is the noun that follows, and 'free' is its quality.

not a part: A truncated quality word ('homogamous') from 'homogamous spikelet pairs' in Andropogoneae. The bearer is the spikelet pair (spikelet PO_0009051). Homogamous is the opposite of heterogamous (FLOPO:0991178) and should be a value term, not a part.

Two senses in the data: the leaf-cell network of mosses (Ephemerum: lax, firm, dense) and the vein areolation of vascular leaves (Buchenavia: prominent). The 2026-11-13 review rejected 'areole' as generic for the same reason.
not a part: A unit of mass (milligram). The bearer is the seed or embryo that is weighed. Same treatment as 'μm' and 'kg' in the 2026-11-13 review.
Two unrelated senses: the transverse bars on the achene surface in Eleocharis ('in each longitudinal row'), and the bars on moss peristome teeth (Funaria, Entosthodon).

not a part: The second term of a relative length ('palea 1/2–2/3 the length of the lemma'). The bearer is the palea or glume. This belongs to the equality-and-ratios pattern with lemma (PO_0009037) as the comparison part.

Generic small tooth: it needs the organ it belongs to (leaf margin, calyx, fruit, peristome...). Same as the 2026-11-13 decisions on horn, mucro and lobule. Where the organ is a leaf, leaf lamina tooth (PO_0025518) applies through the margin rule.

A lobe of a lobe of an unnamed organ (pinnule lobes, leaf lobes, petal lobes). Generic part, like 'lateral lobe' and 'lobule' in the previous review. Counts ('with 1-3 secondary lobes') need the lobed organ as container.

not a part: This is the comparison target in 'anthers 1/4-1/2 filament length': a dimension of the filament, not a part. The bearer is the anther and the quality is decreased length towards filament with the ratio bounds. The 'amount' readings are wrong.
Generic projecting rim or wing (equatorial flange of seeds or fruits, flanges of spores, stem flanges). It needs the organ it belongs to, like wing, ridge and crest in the previous review.

not a part: A position in a series ('outer 5', 'outer 3 sepals', 'les extérieurs'). The part itself (sepal, phyllary, tepal) is elided or comes next. This is a fragment of a position phrase and could become a bearer_quality context word together with its noun.

The margin of a lobe of an unnamed organ (leaf, liverwort leaf lobe, keel, labellum). Both 'lobe' and 'margin' are generic without their organ (see the previous review). Where the clause names the leaf, leaf lamina lobe (PO_0025517) plus the margin region applies.

The middle lobe of an organ that is not named: orchid labellum, corolla lip, leaf, staminode. Same as 'lateral lobe' in the previous review. When the whole is labellum, labellum lobe (FLOPO_0986028) applies through the organ.

not a part: This phrase names the container of a count ('flowers 4-5 per head'), not a part. It matches 'per node', 'per flower' and 'per cluster' from the previous review. 'head' already maps to capitulum inflorescence.

not a part: A position adjective whose noun (awn, papillae, lobes, flowers) follows or is elided ('4 apical'). Same as 'basal' and 'lateral' in the previous review. The region reading is already the 'apically' context word.

A wrong singular form of calli. 'callus' and 'calli' were already rejected as generic parts that need their organ (labellum, petal claw, lemma). Do not use PO_0005052 plant callus, which is undifferentiated tissue. Fix the singular form in the pipeline.
not a part: An adjective (quality), not a structure. The noun 'horn' was rejected as generic. The statements say that some organ's apex bears a horn, which needs that organ.
not a part: A wrong singular form of the quality 'inconspicuous'. The counted part is the noun that follows (veins, ribs, transverse veins). Fix the singular form in the pipeline.
not a part: The container phrase of a count ('2-4 in a cluster'). 'cluster' and 'per cluster' were rejected before because the cluster's kind (fascicle, glomerule, cyme) is not stated.

A generic name for a tine of something forked (a thorn, style, stigma or apex). Like 'arm' and 'segment' in the 2026-11-13 review, it needs the organ it belongs to; the count is better read as a forked or divided quality of that organ.

not a part: A position adjective (on the commissure, the inner face where two mericarps meet), not a part. The part is the following noun: vitta (FLOPO_0986042) or vascular bundle (PO_0005020). Treat it like 'lateral' and 'basal' in the previous review.

not a part: A relative measure ('3/4 length of leaf'): the bearer is the part being described (petiole, sheath), and the leaf is only the thing it is compared with. 'fraction' was rejected as not a structure on 2026-11-13.

not a part: A 'per X' counting phrase; the counted part is the flower. Same as 'per node', 'per axil' and 'per cluster' in the previous review. Note: in these floras (Urticaceae, Amaranthaceae) a glomerule is a dense cluster of flowers, so the PO synonym on compound capitulum inflorescence (PO_0030122) would ground it wrongly.

PO gives 'barb' as a synonym of prickle, thorn, spine leaf and spine stipule. Here it mostly means the small backward-pointing teeth on pappus awns, bristles or spines. Generic: it needs the organ, and the quality is barbed (FLOPO:0991209) or retrorse on that organ.
Generic: the fertile joints of a Salicornia-type spike, of a fern frond, and so on. 'segment' and 'fertile' were both rejected on 2026-11-13; it needs the organ.
not a part: A position in a whorl or series (inner sepals, inner bracts); the part is the noun it qualifies or the elided subject. Treat it like 'primary' and 'lateral' in the previous review.
not a part: A relative width ('1/6–1/3 the width of the leaves'); the leaf is only the thing compared with. See 'fraction'.
not a part: A quality: hyaline is a synonym of PATO_0000964 transparent. The part is the hairpoint, awn or appendage that follows.
not a part: A rank or size adjective (major veins, major lateral lobes); the part is the noun that follows. Treat it like 'primary' and 'secondary'.
A generic narrow connecting part (between leaf lobes, mericarps, fruit segments or anther halves); it needs the organ it belongs to.
Same as 'lateral lobe', rejected on 2026-11-13: generic, it needs the organ (lip, corolla, leaf).

Small rounded teeth on whatever organ is described (petal or ligule apex, margin). Generic: it needs the organ. Only on a leaf is it leaf lamina crena (PO_0025519); otherwise read it as a crenulate quality of that organ.
not a part: A branching event or pattern ('1–3 times dichotomous'), i.e. the number of forkings of the rachis or axis. A quality of that axis, not a part.
General part that needs the organ it belongs to (stigmatic knob, a knob-like perigonium, knobs on a surface). Same as the earlier rejections of crest, horn and callus. A knob-like shape is a quality.

Variant of verticil (whorl). Here it means whorls of flowers in an inflorescence, not the phyllome whorl of PO_0025023. 'whorl' was rejected earlier as a general part that needs its organ, and this follows that decision.
General part that needs its organ (calyx, lemma, leaf apex). Same as the earlier rejection of 'lateral lobe'.

Means cross-bars in several unrelated structures (moss peristome teeth, Isoetes velum, cells), so it needs its organ. For moss peristome teeth, 'trabeculae present' can already be written as peristome tooth (PO_0030043) + trabecular (PATO_0002121).
not a part: The number of turns of a coiled peduncle or fruit is a shape quality of that part (coiled, with n turns), not a separate structure.
not a part: 'ridged' is a quality. The examples are about 'ridges', which were rejected earlier as a general part that needs its organ.
not a part: '3-angular' counts angles (pattern 03). Add 'angular -> angle' to config/flora_counted_parts.tsv next to 'angled'. 'angular ribs' is just an adjective.
not a part: '5-foliate' counts leaflets (pattern 03), like 'foliolate'. Add 'foliate -> leaflet' to config/flora_counted_parts.tsv.
Ambiguous: anther cap (already FLOPO_0986034), root cap, calyptra, seed cap, adaxial cap of cells. It needs the organ it belongs to.
General raised part on a petal, seed or surface, so it needs its organ. Same as knob and crest.
not a part: '4-6-sided' is a shape (number of faces or edges), and 'side branches' is a fragment. Not a structure.
'rib' was rejected earlier as a general part that needs its organ. 'Lateral' does not change that.
not a part: This is a ratio to another part ('aril 1/3 the length of the seed'), pattern 10. The bearer is the aril or lobe, and seed (PO_0009010) is the second part.
not a part: A length quality ('long hairs', 'teeth 5 long and 5 short'). The bearer is the noun that follows.
not a part: A quality of the following noun (ribs, veins, processes).
not a part: A position, already a 'surface' context word in config/flora_context_words.tsv. The part is the noun next to it (spines, stereid bands).
not a part: A ring-shaped quality of the following noun (disc, nectary disc, scar).
General part that needs its organ (spore, bark, fruit apex). Same as the earlier rejections of slit and groove.
General blister-like raised part on a leaf, fruit or thallus. It needs its organ, and some examples may come from lichens, which are not plants. Being pustulate or warty is a quality of the organ.
not a part: A counting modifier ('1-2 additional pairs'). The counted part is the noun that follows it.
not a part: A measure of a structure's height in rows of cells, not a part. The bearer is the structure being described.
not a part: A shape quality that comes before the counted noun (leaves, glands).
not a part: A length ratio to the lobes (pattern 10, ratio to another part), not a part.
not a part: A shape quality of glands; the part is the gland.
Generic part that needs the organ it belongs to (stigma, sarcotesta, seed, perforated leaf blade), as with pore and perforation.
not a part: A size or development quality of the part that follows (leaves, ray flowers, stamens).
Generic part that needs the organ it belongs to, as with terminal lobe and basal lobe in the previous review.
Generic part that needs the organ it belongs to (disc, appendage, scale).
not a part: A width quality of the part that follows (teeth, arms, lobes).
not a part: A measure of width in cells, not a part.
not a part: A shape quality of the part that follows (bracteoles, arms, cystoliths).
not a part: A structural quality, or the bare word segment, which was already rejected as a generic part.
not a part: A position quality of the part that follows (vein, plicae).
Ambiguous: it can mean the rays of a compound umbel (second order inflorescence axis, PO_0006321) or the arms of stellate hairs. The text alone does not say which.

PO tubercle (PO_0025352) is specifically the cactus podarium, but most uses here are generic warts on fruits, seeds or stems. It is a generic part that needs its organ; the bare surface reading is the quality tuberculate.
not a part: The number of branching orders is a quality of the branched structure (inflorescence or shoot), not a part.
not a part: A shape quality of the part that follows (spine, secondary veins).
Plural of apiculum. Generic part that needs its organ, as with apiculus and apiculum in the previous review.
Ambiguous: it could be stipular spines (spine stipule, PO_0025174), spines at the base of a phyllary, or spines on a fruit. The organ is needed.
not a part: A distributive word ('1 between each pair', 'of 4-9 each'), not a structure. The count belongs to the part named elsewhere in the sentence.
A generic outgrowth that needs the organ it belongs to, as 'appendage' was rejected in the previous review.

not a part: A fragment made by a tokenizer or lemmatizer, which ran 'receptacle'/'receptacular' into 'cleistogamous'. The statements are about the receptacle (PO_0009064) and receptacular setae, so fix the matching step instead of adding a rule for this string.

Not the central cell of the embryo sac. The examples ('single large central cell', 'encircling a group of 4-15 small cells', 'isodiametric') describe central cells of different structures (scales, glands, moss areolation). The whole depends on context.
not a part: A shape quality, circular (PATO_0000411). The bearers are the glands and scars named next to it.
Rows of what (cells, scales, hairs, flowers) is not said. A generic arrangement word that needs the organ it belongs to.
not a part: '2-5-pinnate', '4-pinnate' state how many times a leaf is divided. That is a quality of the leaf (pinnate, PATO_0000410, with a count, pattern 03), not a part.
not a part: A shape quality, filiform (PATO_0104351). The bearers are the appendages, tails and processes named next to it.

Covers both the lobes of a divided blade (leaf lamina lobe, PO_0025517) and the leaflets or pinnae of a compound leaf (leaflet, PO_0020049). 'Jamais articulées' and 'primary divisions' point different ways. The right class depends on the flora and the leaf.

Ambiguous without context. The counts ('2-4 hyaline, oblong distal cells') are the upper cells of moss axillary hairs (compare PO_0030062 gametophore axillary hair terminal cell). 'Smooth', 'quadrate' and 'thin' describe the distal cells of the leaf blade. The word alone cannot tell which.

not a part: A suffix for the number of cell layers ('1-stratose', '2-3-stratose'). It is a count word like 'seriate' (rejected 2026-11-13). It belongs as a counted-part entry (stratose -> cell layer) or as unistratose/bistratose values (compare uniseriate FLOPO:0991090), not as a bearer.

not a part: A count phrase ('needles 2 per bundle', 'stamens 3-14 per bundle'), like 'per node' and 'per cluster', which were rejected 2026-11-13. The bundle is the container of a count, and the counted part is the bearer.
French 'dent' = tooth. Like 'lobe', 'segment' and the other generic parts (2026-11-13), it needs the organ it belongs to: calyx tube teeth, bract teeth and others appear among the examples.
not a part: A count phrase ('papillae 1 per lumen', '2-3 per lumen'), like 'per cell' (rejected 2026-11-13). The lumen is the container of the count, not a bearer.
not a part: French 'rang' means row or series. 'sur 2 rangs' or 'étamines sur 4 rangs' is a count of rows: an arrangement of the parts named in the same sentence, not a part itself.

A generic outgrowth that needs the organ it sits on. The previous review rejected protuberance and projection the same way. 'with warts' is better annotated as PATO_0001361 warty on the bearing organ. Some 'white circular warts' on branchlets may be lenticels (PO_0000031), but that cannot be told without context.
not a part: '3 cell layers thick' and 'medulla a single cell layer' give a thickness counted in cells. It is a measure of the named part, not a part of its own.
not a part: A fragment of a ratio statement ('palea 2/3 as long as lemma'). This is pattern 10 (ratio to another part), with lemma (PO_0009037) as the other part. It is not a part.
not a part: A fragment of ratio statements ('petals 1/3-2/3 as long as sepals'). This is pattern 10, with sepal (PO_0009031) as the other part.
A generic part that needs the organ it belongs to. It covers spadix appendix threads, filament-like appendages and fibres, and the examples do not say which.
not a part: A fragment of a compound count word ('3-6-nate at the lower nodes' = branches in whorls of 3-6). This is pattern 03 (count of parts) for branches per node.
Ambiguous. French 'partitions pennatifides' are divisions of a parted leaf, 'cloisons saillantes' are septa, and 'partitions between the anther holes' are anther septa (PO_0005010). It needs context.
French 'appendice' = appendage, a generic part (previous review rejected 'appendage'); examples range over corolla lip appendages and glandular appendages of different organs.

These are lobes/appendages of the inflorescence receptacle of Dorstenia-type Moraceae; PO receptacle (PO_0009064) is the flower receptacle, and whether the lobes are bracts is not settled. Ambiguous without a class for the inflorescence receptacle.
not a part: Fragment of a ratio to another part ('1/3 as long as bracts'): pattern 10, the bract (PO_0009055 family) is the second term, not a bearer.
not a part: A density (count of marginal teeth per unit length); the part is the teeth of the margin, 'per cm' is a unit fragment.
not a part: Fragment of a ratio to another part ('1.5-2 x as long as sepals'): pattern 10.
not a part: Ratio of two dimensions of the bearer: pattern 11.
The examples ('proximal 2.5-3 mm cream-colored', 'vestigial pistillode bases', 'longitudinally ridged') do not show which structure is meant; ambiguous without context.

not a part: A counting unit in moss descriptions ('2-stratose in 1-3 cell rows', 'of 4-6 rows of cells'): the number of cell rows is a width measure of the border or costa that is being described. The bearer is that border or costa, and the number of rows is its quality; 'cell row' is not a bearer itself.

'Appendage' of the corolla covers different structures: faucal scales or fornices (Boraginaceae, which could go to corolline corona FLOPO_0985021), infrastaminal scales, spurs and appendages of the lobes. The examples (2 or 2-4 appendages, multicellular, linear to conical) do not tell which one is meant. A floral corona class would be a doubtful target without the family.
not a part: Part of an arrangement phrase ('flowers 7-9 per spiral'). The bearer is the flower and the count is per spiral of the axis.
not a part: French 'or' (alternatives, pattern 07), not a word for a plant part.
not a part: A unit, not a part: overlap, moisture content, viability.
not a part: Part of a count phrase ('lateral nerves up to 8 on either side of the midrib'). The bearer is the vein and 'on either side' says how it is counted.
not a part: A bad split of the French 'fois' (times), as in '2 fois bifurqué' and '3-4 fois ramifiées'. It is a degree of branching or division, or a ratio, not a part.
not a part: A quality of arrangement (crowded pairs of pinnae or leaflets), not a part.
not a part: Part of a ratio to another part ('2 times as long as the sepals'), handled by pattern 10 with sepal (PO_0009031) as the other part.

'Lip' is either the corolla lip (FLOPO_0985017, sympetalous families) or the orchid labellum (a petal; there is no labellum class, only labellum lobe FLOPO_0986028). 'Limb' is then the expanded blade of either. The examples (semiorbicular, dentate, 3-4 mm) do not tell which family.
'scale' on its own was rejected as a generic part in the previous review. A lobe of an unnamed scale has the same problem: the organ that bears it (bract, hair, ligule, perianth scale) is missing.
Ambiguous. It can be an apical beak of a fruit, a leftover style base, a central column or a stump left on a stem ('leaving a small peg'). It cannot be placed without the organ.

A wart-like outgrowth with no organ named, the same problem as 'rib' and 'scale' in the previous review. Warts on a named organ are better recorded as that organ with the quality warty (PATO:0001361).
not a part: A phrase fragment that gives the unit of a count ('1-2 at each node'). The counted part comes before it; the stem node (PO_0020141) is only the place where it is counted.

Ambiguous between a disc-shaped fused androecium (synandrium FLOPO_0986014, e.g. Myristicaceae) and a floral disc next to the stamens (FLOPO_0986025). The hairy and hirsute statements fit both. It needs the family to decide.
not a part: A fragment: the second term of a ratio ('neck 1/2-1 times urn length', pattern 10). The part it refers to is the urn, sporangium theca (PO_0030041), and length is the quality.
not a part: A fragment that gives the unit of a count ('12-18 per row'); the counted part comes before it.
not a part: A quality. The part follows it ('persistent styles', 'persistent sheath').

not a part: A quality: pendent (PATO_0104035, which the union-pair config already uses). It was caught together with its count. The bearer is the branch that follows ('2 pendent branches', Sphagnum branch fascicles).
not a part: A position word ('abaxial spines', 'abaxial and adaxial'). The noun it qualifies is missing; this is a fragment.
not a part: A shape or arrangement word ('ring of hairs', 'anneau de poils'), not a structure. The bare 'ring' was already rejected as a generic part.
not a part: An adverb modifying 'stalked' or 'petiolulate'. A fragment.

'Filament' here is not the stamen filament: these are cell rows ('filaments of 4-8 cells', with papillae per cell), as on moss leaves or on staminal hairs. Which filament is meant cannot be told without context.
Generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to ('bracteate units', 'phloem units').

Consistent with the earlier rejection of 'areole' as generic. Where the head is a leaf or lamina, leaf lamina areole (PO_0025392) applies, but here some uses are on other organs ('400-500 areolae on each side').
Generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to. The singular 'cell' was rejected in the previous review.
Generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to. Compare the earlier rejection of 'lateral lobe'.

PO tubercle (PO_0025352) is the cactus podarium, but floras use 'tubercles' for wart-like outgrowths on seeds, fruits, stems and leaves. Without the organ the meaning is unclear; on a known organ, 'tuberculate' as a quality is better.
not a part: A shape quality of hairs or scales ('stellate hairs', 'stellate scales'); the noun is missing.
not a part: A measurement used as the second term of a relative length ('leaves 1/2-2/3 of stem length'). The bearer is the leaf and the reference is the stem (PO_0009047).
Generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to. This follows the earlier rejection of 'callus'. Callosities occur on orchid lips, legume standards, fruits and leaf margins.
not a part: A shape word, not a part: subulate is PATO:0001954, and the part it describes is the process, projection or gland named next to it. French 'subules' is the same quality used as a noun.

A scar of unstated origin (leaf, stipule, bract, seed hilum). It is the same as 'scar', which the 11-13 review rejected as a generic part. When the context says it is a leaf scar, use leaf scar (FLOPO_0986052).
A generic part that needs the organ it belongs to: staminiferous pockets of a corolla or corona, inner pockets, pockets formed by lobes. Like 'sac' and 'cavity' in the previous review.
A cell wall inside a peltate scale (trichome). It is a generic part that needs its whole, and PO has no peltate-scale class to attach it to. The count only makes sense together with the scale.
A cell wall of a peltate scale, same case as 'radial wall'. Generic part without a class for its whole.
not a part: A grouping word ('in 2 unequal sets'), not a structure. The count belongs to the stamens or nerves being grouped.
not a part: A position fragment ('8-15 in marginal row'). The counted part (cells, glands, flowers) comes before it.
not a part: A pronoun from 'to 1/3 its length', and once the OCR of 'µm' ('30-40 it long'). Not a structure.
A generic opening that needs the organ it belongs to: a mericarp, a pitcher or corolla mouth, a spathe. Like 'opening' in the previous review. It is not the stomatal pore.
not a part: A position fragment ('widest 1/3-1/2 from base'). It gives where along the bearer a value holds, not a part.
not a part: A quality, not a part. 'Megaspores of 2 sizes' says the megaspores are unequal in size (FLOPO_0991101 unequal).
not a part: An adjective for having lamellae, not a part. The noun 'lamella' was rejected as a generic part on 11-13.
not a part: A quality (split or divided), with its count of divisions, of a peristome tooth, a nerve or a leaf.
not a part: A shape quality of the glands, appendages or head it describes.
Mixed senses: French 'lanières' are narrow lobes or segments of a leaf or perianth, while 'median stripe' is a colour pattern. Without context it cannot be grounded.

A burr is a dispersal unit with hooked spines, but what it is varies by taxon: a fruit, an involucre of bristles round spikelets (Cenchrus), or a whole cyme or infructescence ('each cyme falls as a complete burr'). Only 'present' is stated. Without the taxon it cannot be grounded to one class.
not a part: A unit of length (µm; 'fi' and '/*' are OCR of µ). It belongs with the measurement, as 'μm' did in the previous review.
not a part: A quality, FLOPO:0991078 pinnatifid. '2–3-pinnatifid' is its degree, not a part to count.
not a part: A unit of time (leaf life span, flowering and maturation periods, chilling requirement). It is not a plant structure.
not a part: An adverb, a fragment of 'pairs of strongly ascending nerves'. The counted part is the vein.

A narrow segment of whatever organ is being described: calyx or corolla lobes (often in Flora do Brasil), leaf segments or perianth segments. It is generic, like 'segment', which the previous review rejected because it needs the organ it belongs to.
not a part: A quality (PATO:0104355 ascending), a fragment of 'ascending teeth' or 'ascending lateral veins'.
not a part: A row is an arrangement of other parts (scales, cells, spines, seeds). The number of rows is a quality of what is arranged in them, and that part must come from the statement.
not a part: A quality (blunt or obtuse), a fragment of 'blunt ridges' or 'blunt angles'. The counted part is the ridge or angle.
not a part: A length-to-width ratio phrase, not a structure. It is handled like 'ratio' in the previous review.
not a part: The degree of branching of an inflorescence or axis is a quality of the branched structure, not a part. The bearer is the inflorescence or axis named in the statement.
not a part: A counting context ('bracts 1–2 per pedicel'), like 'per node' and 'per flower' in the previous review. The counted part is the bract or bracteole.
not a part: A positional quality (on the side toward the base of the rachis), a fragment of 'basiscopic pinnules' or 'basiscopic nerves'. The counted part is the pinnule or vein.
not a part: A shape quality (conical), a fragment of 'conic prickles' or 'conic projection'. The part is the prickle or projection.

An auricle of whatever organ is being described: the leaf base, stipules, a grass sheath (PO_0020106 leaf sheath auricle covers only that case) or a calyx or corolla. It is generic and needs the organ it belongs to, like 'claw' and 'horn' in the previous review.
not a part: A fragment of '3-sect' or '3–5-sect', meaning dissected into that many segments: PATO:0104362 dissected (or FLOPO pinnatisect when pinnate). It is a quality, not a part.
not a part: A colour word cut off from 'dark veins', 'dark glands' and 'dark ribs'; the part is the noun that follows it.
not a part: A modifier cut off from 'principal vein' and 'principal lateral veins'; the part is the vein.
Ambiguous: the examples mix a legume keel (PO_0025327, two fused petals) with the keel of a liverwort leaf ('keel apex and postical lobe margin'). Without the flora it cannot be grounded.
Generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to. A 'glandular patch' is a gland (portion of secretory tissue PO_0005656) on the part that bears it.
not a part: A modifier cut off from 'interstitial veins' (short veins between the secondaries); the part is the vein (higher order leaf vein PO_0008023 at most).

not a part: A fragment of a seed count with its container: 'seeds 1-2 per pod', '3-6-seeded' (pod). The counted part is seed (PO_0009010) and the container is legume fruit (PO_0030100, synonym 'pod') or follicle fruit (PO_0030105, also synonym 'pod'), pattern 03. 'per pod' is not a structure, the same as 'per node' and 'per pinna' last time.

not a part: A proportion of a part's length over which it is connate, divided or toothed ('connate 3/5-2/3 their lengths', 'soudés sur 1/5-2/5 de leur longueur'). This is the extent of a quality, like 'fraction' rejected last time, not a structure.

not a part: The arrangement of ovules or seeds within a locule ('seeds in 2 rows per locule', '2-4 rangées d'ovules par loge'). A row is a series (seriation), not a structure. The parts are seed (PO_0009010) or ovule, held in plant ovary locule (PO_0025266) or fruit locule (PO_0025270). It is like 'seeds per locule' and 'seriate' last time.

'segment' was rejected last time as a generic part that needs its organ. The stalk of a segment ('leaving persistent stalk', 'dark color', 0.6-1.5 mm) cannot be placed without knowing whether the segment is a leaf segment, a perianth segment or a fruit article. stalk (PO_0025066) alone would lose the whole it belongs to.

not a part: An adjective fragment of 'antheridial buds' or 'antheridial branch' (moss perigonia). The structure behind it is antheridium (PO_0025125) or a male branch or bud, which the tokenizer should take as a phrase. The word alone is not a part.
not a part: An adverb from 'closely set' or 'closely spaced'. It is a degree of the spacing of the counted pinnae or leaflets, not a structure.

not a part: A texture or structure quality of a root system, tunic or sheath remnants ('fibrous root cluster', 'remnant fibrous sheaths'). The bearers are root system (PO_0025025), tunic (FLOPO_0986041) and similar. It is not a part.

not a part: A quality word (stipitate). The examples measure the stipe itself, and 'stipe' already has a rule to stalk (PO_0025066, C264). Like 'beaked', 'clawed' and 'pedicellate' last time, it names no structure.

not a part: A row is an arrangement of the counted parts, not a structure ('2 or 3 rows of areoles', '25 rangées'). It is the same as 'rows per locule'. The part itself, areole, was rejected last time because it is ambiguous (cactus areole vs leaf lamina areole PO_0025392). Counts of rows are seriation, which pattern 03 does not split.

'segment' is a generic part (rejected last review, as were 'terminal segment', 'lateral segment' and 'basal lobe'). The basal segments of a leaf, a pinna or a perianth cannot be told apart without the organ.
not a part: A shape modifier ('broadly triangular', 'broadly ovate'). The counted parts are lobes, leaflets or teeth. It is a degree of a quality, not a structure.
not a part: A quality (visibility or prominence) of leaf scars, midvein, lenticels or hilum. Like 'prominent' last time, it is not a structure.

not a part: A positional quality ('median row of large cells', 'median chlorocysts'). Some examples are elliptic fragments ('2 median distinct') whose part is elsewhere in the sentence. It is not a structure.
not a part: A texture quality of a sheath or membrane ('membranous sheath', 'gaines membraneuses'). The bearer is the sheath. It is not a part.

not a part: A fragment of 'vascular bundle' ('base with 4 vascular bundles' in fern stipes). That phrase is already vascular bundle (PO_0005020); the fix is to take the two words as one term. The adjective alone is not a part.

In ferns, the lobe or pinnule on the side of a pinna that faces its base. 'lobe' is a generic part (rejected last review). The examples mix lobes of pinnae with basiscopic pinnules ('1-3 basiscopical pinnules'), and no pattern covers the basiscopic or acroscopic position. A class for it would be doubtful.
not a part: A quality (elevated or prominent) of the counted veins or glands ('8-10 raised veins'). It is not a structure.
A generic region ('forming a zone', '2 zones glanduleuses latérales'). It needs the organ and the kind of zone, the same as band, spot and layer last review.

not a part: The second term of a ratio ('awn 1-2 times the length of the lemma', 'palea 1 length of lemma'). This is pattern 10, ratio to another part, with the lemma as the other part. It is a fragment like 'times calyx' last time.

The plural of 'areole', rejected last review as ambiguous. It may be the spine-bearing cushion of a cactus or a mesh of the leaf venation, leaf lamina areole (PO_0025392). 'without areoles' and 'areoles 0.3-2.0 mm' do not tell which.
not a part: A growth form, a quality of the whole plant or colony ('in loose or dense mats', mat-forming), not a part.
not a part: An adjective fragment ('of 1 row of cells', 'formées de cellules'). The part is plant cell (PO_0009002) or the cell layer of the organ in the sentence. The word names no structure.
not a part: A shape word meaning whip-like ('flagelliform branches'). It is not a part. The part is the branch; the word is a quality of that branch.
A group of parts that are not named ('in 2's and 3's', 'groupes de 1-3'). The organ is lost, as with 'cluster' and 'fascicle', which the 2026-11-13 review rejected.

An apiculum sitting just below the tip of some organ that is not named. 'apiculum' and 'apiculus' were rejected as generic parts on 2026-11-13. The only PO apiculus classes are for the palea and the lemma, and nothing shows the organ here.

'Stamens in 2 cycles' means stamen whorls. 'whorl' was rejected as a generic part, and pattern 03 does not split 'seriate' because it names no single part. The count belongs to the stamens' arrangement, not to a structure called 'cycle'.
not a part: A hairiness quality (PATO pubescent). In 'domaties pubescentes' the part is the domatium (FLOPO_0986021).
Without its noun this could be tertiary leaflets, tertiary veins or tertiary branches. 'primary' and 'secondary' were rejected on 2026-11-13 for the same reason.
The front lobe of some organ that is not named (an orchid lip, a perianth limb, a labellum). 'lateral lobe' was rejected as a generic part on 2026-11-13.

'scale' was rejected as a generic part (it could be a bud scale, scale leaf, bract or trichome scale). 'basal' is already a position word that may apply to 'scale' (flora_context_words.tsv). The organ the scale belongs to is still missing.

not a part: A surface feature of some unnamed part, which is a quality: bullate (FLOPO_0991122), or blistered when filled with fluid. 'Oil-filled blisters' may be oil glands, but the organ is not given.
not a part: A piece of a relation ('each bract subtending 3 flowers'), not a part. The count is of flowers (PO_0009046) in a bract's axil.
An appendage of some unnamed organ ('appendage' was rejected as generic). It could be a gland (PO_0005656) on a petal, an anther connective or an involucre gland, and the context does not say which.
not a part: A shape quality ('hooked spur', '5-8 hooked' prickles). The parts are the spur and the prickles.
The cavity of the cells of a lamella. 'lumen' was rejected as a generic part, and 'lamella' could be a moss leaf lamella, a ligule or a gill. One example only.
Two generic parts joined by 'or', with the organ missing (leaf margin, calyx, bract). These are unions of parts, not one structure, and the pair is not in flora_union_pairs.tsv.
A rib of some unnamed organ (fruit, seed, calyx, stem). 'rib' was rejected as a generic part on 2026-11-13. 'Longitudinal' adds the direction but not the organ.
not a part: A broken stem of 'numerous', a count value ('2-numerous pairs'), not a plant part.
not a part: A count unit, like 'per node' and 'per cell' in the previous review. The counted part comes earlier in the sentence and the valve (fruit valve PO_0000033) is only the unit.
not a part: An adverb from 'pinnately lobed' (FLOPO:0991157) or 'pinnately arranged'. It is a quality, not a part.
not a part: A quality: the value class FLOPO:0991047 scarious already exists. The part is the noun after it (margin, appendage).
not a part: An adjective for an extra or secondary member (accessory tubers, accessory veins, accessory lobe). The part is the noun that follows.
A generic part (the previous review rejected 'pore'). It could be an anther pore (PO_0025118), a pore in a capsule, or a pollen aperture. The organ it belongs to is not given.
Wall thickenings in the clear cells of Sphagnum leaves: a cell-wall detail used only in moss treatments, with no PO class. Not worth a new class for now.
not a part: A quality: PATO_0002351 fleshy. The part is the noun after it (scales, disk, appendage).
not a part: A ratio to another part ('1/3-1/2 the length of the tube'), handled by pattern 10. The other part is the corolla tube (FLOPO_0985018) or calyx tube (FLOPO_0986011).
not a part: A ratio to another part ('1/2-2/3 as long as internodes'), handled by pattern 10. The other part is the stem internode (PO_0020142).
not a part: A ratio to another part ('occupying 2/5-3/4 the leaf base'), handled by pattern 10. The other part is the leaf base (PO_0020040) and the quality is width.
not a part: A count ending ('5-parted'). config/flora_counted_parts.tsv already maps 'parted' to lobe (pattern 03).
A generic part (the previous review rejected 'ridge'). Here the ridges are on a stigmatic disk, which the word alone does not say.
not a part: A count of seeds (PO_0009010) per locule. Here 'cell' means locule. Treated like 'seeds per locule' and 'per cell' in the previous review.
not a part: A quality: unbranched or not compound (simple veinlets, simple leaflets).
not a part: An adjective (bristly; setose is PATO_0002289). The noun 'bristle' was rejected earlier as too generic.
not a part: A ratio to another part ('about half as long'), handled by pattern 10. The other part varies (flower, spur, corolla).

Generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to (nutlet appendages in Boraginaceae, hair-like appendages elsewhere); as with 'segment' and 'lumen' in the 2026-11-13 review, no single class fits without context.
not a part: The number of cell layers ('2 layers of cells', '1-stratose') is a thickness or structure quality of the part that has them (exostome tooth, lamina), not a part to annotate.
not a part: Fragment of a comparison ('1/6-1/4 of the leaf length'): it is a ratio of the bearer's length to the leaf, for pattern 10 (ratio to another part), not a part.
not a part: The number of turns of a coil or twist ('5 turns', 'faisant 1-5 tours') is a twisted or coiled quality of the bearer (awn, fruit, tendril), not a part.
not a part: Quality (how many there are) of the structure it qualifies (cystoliths, nectaries).
not a part: Fragment of '-androus' (word trimmed too far). '3-4-androus' counts stamens: add androus -> stamen to the counted-parts table (pattern 03) and do not ground the fragment.
not a part: Quality (depth) of lobes or grooves; the counted part is the lobe or groove.
not a part: Stem fragment of inflorescence(s), also caught on 'ramifications'; fix the word trimming so the full word grounds to inflorescence PO_0009049 rather than adding a rule for the fragment.
not a part: Texture quality of the part it describes (woody rootstock, woody brachyblasts); the bearers are rootstock/rhizome and short shoot, already ruled.
A loose group (young stems, leaves, inflorescences, whatever is not woody) with no single PO class. Shoot system would be too broad and would wrongly include woody stems.
not a part: Fragment of a comparison ('1/3-1/2 the length of the lamina'): a ratio of the bearer's length to the lamina (pattern 10), not a part.
not a part: Arrangement of veins or roots ('veins forming a network'): a reticulate or anastomosing quality (FLOPO:0991128) of the veins, not a part.
not a part: Quality (venation or surface pattern), not a part.
not a part: Number word belonging to a count, not a part.
not a part: How many times something branches ('branching 8-10 times') is a branched quality of the axis or hair, not a part.
not a part: Colour quality of the marks or spots it describes.
not a part: Fragment of a verb phrase ('nerves bearing ... scales'); the scales are the part, and they are already handled by existing bearer rules.

Fruiting body of a lichen (examples: Hypotrachyna, Peltigera, Collema), which is a fungal structure. It is outside the scope of PO and FLOPO, which cover plants, so it should not be grounded or proposed to PO.
not a part: French preposition ('for') in phrases that split a total ('dont 2–3 pour l'acumen', '3 pour l'andropodium'). It is a fragment; the real part is the noun after it.
not a part: A 'per X' phrase giving the container of a count ('blades 3–6 per fertile culm'). Not a structure; the container is stem (PO_0009047) and 'fertile' is its state.
not a part: A broken lemmatization of 'spore radius', used as a unit in a ratio ('proximal laesura less than 0.4 spore radius'). It is a measure, not a structure.
not a part: A 'per X' phrase giving the container of a count ('stems 1 per caudex branch'). The container is stem (PO_0009047, caudex synonym).

not a part: A fragment of a ratio ('basal membrane 1/2 exostome height'): the bearer is the endostome basal membrane, and exostome height is the reference dimension (pattern 10, ratio to another part; peristome PO_0030042).
not a part: The French preposition 'de' ('4 mm de long'), a parsing fragment.
not a part: A fragment giving the scope of a count ('nectaries 2 per corolla lobe'). The bearer is the nectary; the corolla lobe (FLOPO_0986006) is only the reference.

not a part: A fragment ('cystoliths present') naming a calcium carbonate concretion inside a cell (a cell inclusion, a substance), not a PO plant structure. Better handled later as presence of cystoliths on the leaf, not as a bearer class.
Ambiguous: bladder traps, vesicular hairs, inflated fruiting structures ('with dentate foliaceous e...') or cell inclusions in different floras.

not a part: Location fragment of a count ('vittae 2 on commissure'); the counted part is vitta (FLOPO_0986042), the commissure face is a container, not a bearer. Same treatment as the 'per ...' fragments.
not a part: Count fragment ('flowers 1-4 per ocreate fascicle'); a container phrase like the rejected 'per node', 'per axil'.
not a part: Location fragment of a count ('vittae 1 in each furrow'); counted part is vitta (FLOPO_0986042), the furrow is the container.
not a part: Count fragment ('pinnae 20-30 per side of rachis'), as the rejected 'per side'; also a mis-singularised 'rachis'.
not a part: Fragment of a ratio or measure ('up to 5 [m / times] height of plant'); height is a quality and the plant is already whole plant, so this is not a part name.
not a part: Ratio fragment ('petals 2.5-3 × as long as calyx'); calyx is the reference part of pattern 10 (ratio to another part), not a new bearer.

'Appendage' was rejected as a generic part in the previous review. On a perianth it can be a wing, spine, tubercle or scale (e.g. the fruiting perianth of Chenopodiaceae), so the structure is not determined. The perianth (PO_0009058) is the whole, but there is no class or pattern for an unspecified outgrowth.

not a part: A fragment: it names the container of a count ('pseudospikelets 1 per spathe'), as were 'per node', 'per bract' and 'per flower'. The counted part is the bearer; spathe (FLOPO_0986007) is the whole.
not a part: A fragment: it names the container of a count ('nuts 3 per cupule'), like 'per node' and 'per bract'. The counted part is the bearer; cupule (FLOPO_0986036) is the whole.
not a part: A fragment with a negation. It states that bulbils (FLOPO_0986055) are absent, which belongs to the absence pattern (bulbil + absent), not to a new part.

not a part: An adjective from a count word ('4-8-rayed' = with 4-8 rays of an umbel or pseudumbel), handled by the count-of-parts pattern. It is not a part name, like 'foliolate' and 'seriate' before.

not a part: A measured dimension (length of the leaf lamina, PO_0020039), not a structure; the examples are ratios to the leaf (pattern 10) or vein-extent statements. Same as the earlier 'leaf length' decision.
not a part: A 'per X' counting phrase (sori per ultimate leaf segment), not a structure. The earlier review rejected 'per segment' and 'ultimate segment' in the same way.

not a part: French 'pair', a counting unit ('3 paires de folioles' = 6 leaflets in 3 pairs); count of parts (pattern 03; cf. 'jugate' in flora_counted_parts). The earlier review rejected 'pair' as not a structure.
not a part: A ratio to another part (pattern 10), not a structure. The other part, the trophophore, is the sterile blade of an Ophioglossaceae leaf.

A pore in the wall of a Sphagnum hyaline cell. PO has no hyaline cell (hyalocyst) and a wall pore is not a PO-kind structure. Most statements are counts per cell (see 'pores per cell'). Revisit only together with a hyaline cell class.
The female gametangium of Characeae or Vaucheria (algae), outside PO's scope. Mapping it to a land-plant gametangium class would be doubtful.
Unclear: the persistent remains of perianth, style or stamens on the fruit. Which organ it is cannot be told without context; persistence should go on that organ.
not a part: A count of seeds (PO_0009010) per fruit valve (PO_0000033), not a structure; same as the earlier 'seeds per locule'.
not a part: A count phrase (Sphagnum hyaline-cell pores per cell), not a structure; same as the earlier 'per cell'.
A generic part ('wing' was rejected on 2026-11-13) that needs the organ it belongs to. It could be a wing of a fruit, a mericarp rib, a seed or a calyx. 'Dorsal' gives a position, not the organ.
not a part: A shape quality (acicular) of the spines or hairs that follow it ('needlelike spines on costa'). The bearer is the noun after it.
not a part: A rate of flowering ('flowers 1 opening per day'). The bearer is the flower and the statement is about timing, not a structure.
not a part: The second term of a ratio ('2--3 x as long as perianth'). Use pattern 10 (equality and ratio to another part), with perianth PO_0009058 as the other part.
'Segment' was rejected as a generic part, so its margin is generic too. It could be the margin of a perianth segment, a leaf segment or a frond segment.

not a part: A count of branches per node: the part is a branch, and 'per node' only says where they are counted ('per node' was rejected on 2026-11-13). Use pattern 03 (count of parts) with stem node PO_0020141, or inflorescence axis for a rachis.
not a part: A colour mark ('red dots basally'): a spotted colour pattern of the petal or tepal, not a structure. The bearer is the organ the dots are on.

A misspelling of areola or areole. In these examples it reads as seed-coat reticulum cells ('ca. 50 longitudinal rows', 'end walls raised'), but the organ is not given. 'Areole' was rejected as generic.

Ambiguous: it could be the bracts of a fruiting catkin ('those at middle of cones', as in Betulaceae: inflorescence bract), cone scales (megasporophyll PO_0009027), or scales on a fruit surface ('bristly', 'fringed'). These need different targets.
A generic swelling that needs the organ it belongs to, like 'protuberance' in the previous review. The quality reading is FLOPO gibbous.
not a part: A clustered calcium oxalate crystal inside a cell: a mineral inclusion (substance), not an anatomical part. PO has no crystal classes.
Plural of 'scale', which the previous review rejected as a generic part that needs its organ (trichome scale, bract or scale leaf).
An order of division without its organ, like 'primary segment' and 'ultimate segment', which were rejected as generic.

not a part: 'Costa ending 2-6 cells before apex' gives how far the costa stops short of the leaf tip, measured in cells. It is a fragment of a position statement on the costa (PO_0030072), not a part.
not a part: A fragment of a count phrase ('flowers ca. 3 visible per spiral'); the counted part is the flower, the spiral its series. Like the rejected 'per node' and 'per whorl'.
not a part: Crystals (calcium oxalate, alongside tannin) are cell contents (substances), not anatomical parts. PO has none.

The word means different things in different groups: a stalk-like base in some ferns, a false stalk in mosses, and in algae and fungi. The examples don't show which one. Mapping it to stalk (PO_0025066) would be a guess.
not a part: A piece of 'second pair (of pinnae)'. It gives a place in a series, not a part; the part is pinna. Same as 'secondary' in the previous review.
not a part: A unit of length: the old line (ligne), about 2.1-2.3 mm, as in '2-3 lin. thick'. It belongs in the unit table, not the parts list.
not a part: A piece of a counting phrase ('2 in the cluster'). 'per cluster' and 'cluster' were already rejected.
not a part: The second half of a relative length ('Embryo 0.2 length of caryopsis'). The bearer is the embryo (PO_0009009) and the caryopsis is what it is compared with; this is not a part.
Without context, 'shell' can mean the whole wall of a nut (pericarp PO_0009084), the stone of a drupe (endocarp PO_0009086), or a hard seed coat (testa PO_0020057). The flora decides which.

A raised rim around the chalaza of a seed. Mapping it to seed chalaza (PO_0006333) would turn 'collar present' into 'chalaza present', which is always true. Only 2 floras use it, too few for a new class.

not a part: A substance: a mealy waxy powder given off on fern fronds and Primula leaves. 'abaxially with white farina' should be read as the quality mealy (PATO_0104364) on the underside of the frond or leaf.
not a part: A narrowing of a fruit between its seeds (as in loments), not a part in its own right. '8-12 constrictions on each side' is a count of the quality constricted (PATO_0001847) on the fruit.
not a part: A quality, exserted (PATO_0000623), which got split off its noun ('3-4 exserted valves').
In moss floras (e.g. Pohlia) the 'primordia' are the small leaves at the tip of a bulbil, not a young bulbil. Neither bulbil (FLOPO_0986055) nor leaflet primordium fits, so a mapping would be wrong.
not a part: The second half of a relative length ('basal membrane 1/4-1/2 exostome length'). The bearer is the other part.

PO has no cell wall class (cell walls are in GO), and the examples don't say which organ's margin is meant (moss leaf, leaf border). Thick or pitted walls need a decision on the cell-wall bearer first.

French for 'sheath', which the previous review rejected as a generic part. 'Gaines caulinaires' or 'aphylles' may be leaf sheaths (PO_0020104) or scale leaves (PO_0006003), depending on the group, so give it the same rejection as 'sheath'.
not a part: Degree of branching ('4-5 times branched'): the number of branching orders of the part being described, i.e. the quality branched (PATO:0000402) with a count. It is not a structure.

Ambiguous across families: it can be a connective appendage, a filament appendage or spur, or a staminal corona segment (FLOPO_0985022). Which one is meant depends on the taxon, so there is no single bearer.
The female sex organ of algae (Charophyceae, or brown algae when 'in sori'). This is outside the land-plant scope of PO and FLOPO. A class only makes sense if FLOPO decides to annotate algae.
Generic surface marking with no stated organ. As a surface pattern it is the quality striated rather than a part, and 'not easily deciduous' shows the readings are mixed.

not a part: Adjective fragment of 'stomatal rows'. The statements count rows of stomata (stomatal complex PO_0002000) at a position on the leaf, which is a count per position and is held (pattern 03 limits).
not a part: The second term of a ratio or comparison ('to 1/2 of achene length'). Pattern 10 handles this, with the achene as the other part.

not a part: Fragment: the number of rows of lacunae on each side of the midrib. The lacunae are plant anatomical space (PO_0025117, synonym lacuna), but a count of rows at a position is held (count_per_position), not a new bearer.
Ambiguous: it can be an aril, caruncle (PO_0020060), elaiosome (PO_0020062), wing or tail ('caudate', 'subulate', '1 or 2'). Without the family it cannot be grounded.
not a part: Fragment of 'embryo with 1 full spiral': the number of turns of a coiled embryo, a quality of plant embryo (PO_0009009), not a part.

'scale' is sense-split (floral scale or bract, bud scale, scale leaf, indumentum scale). Probably the midvein of Cyperaceae floral scales, but the organ cannot be fixed without context, and PO has a midvein class only for leaves.
not a part: Position phrase of a count ('veins 4-9 on each side of midrib'). Pattern 03 holds counts per position (count_per_position).

Plural of the generic 'wing', which was rejected before. The readings mix wing petals ('wings and keel pale lemon yellow', 'clawed' → wing petal PO_0025325) with petiole and rachis wings ('stipels or wings').
Generic 'layer' with only a side given. The organ and tissue are unknown (likely a bryophyte leaf or stem layer), so it cannot be grounded.
not a part: Position phrase of a count ('areolae 5-7 across the face'). It is a count per position, held by pattern 03.

not a part: '0-1-septate' is a compound count word like '5-nerved'. It gives the number of cross-walls in a hair, cell or spore. The part is the septum; the bearer comes from the noun it describes ('hyaline cells').
not a part: A position word ('intercalary branches', 'intercalary, sterile ...'): it means inserted between other parts of a series. It describes a state of the part, not a part.

not a part: Raphides are needle-shaped calcium oxalate crystals inside cells: a substance in a cell, not a plant part. This follows the decision on 'crystal'. The cell that holds them is an idioblast (PO_0000283), if a bearer is wanted.
not a part: A size word ('4 tiny teeth', 'tiny leaflets'). The counted part is the noun after it (tubercle, tooth, leaflet).
not a part: 'Petals 1.5-2 times as long as sepals' compares lengths. The bearer is the subject of the sentence (petal, pedicel). The sepal is the second part of the comparison, not a new part.

not a part: 'Flowers 10-20 in whorls' counts the subject (flowers, leaves) per whorl and says they are whorled. The whorl is the counting unit. If the whorl itself must be a bearer, it is collective phyllome structure (PO_0025023, synonym 'whorl').
not a part: A word that ranks members of a set ('central 3 dominant'), not a part. The counted part is the noun before it (branches).
not a part: A wrinkle is a fold in a surface, not an anatomical part. The surface's quality is wrinkled or rugose, and the count is an extra detail of that quality.
not a part: 'Vein anastomoses 1-3' counts the points where veins join. A joining point is a relation between veins, not a part. The value class for anastomosing veins already exists.
not a part: Fragment: the denominator of a count ('bulbils 1 per frond'). The counted part is the bearer; the frond (FLOPO_0985026) is its whole (pattern 12).
not a part: Fragment: the denominator of a count ('leaves 2 per pseudobulb'); the leaves are the bearer and pseudobulb (FLOPO_0986027) the whole they belong to.
Not a plant structure: micronemata are thin conidiophores of fungi (hyphomycetes), outside PO and FLOPO.
not a part: Fragment: a count of pores per hyaline cell (Sphagnum). The bearer is the hyaline cell's wall pores; 'per cell' is the denominator.
not a part: Fragment: the reference of a ratio ('basal membrane 1/5-1/3 endostome length'); pattern 10, not a bearer.
French 'wing': a generic part that needs the organ it belongs to, as 'wing' in the previous review.
not a part: Substance: bundles of needle-shaped calcium oxalate crystals inside cells. Not a plant structure; the cell that holds them is an idioblast (PO_0000283).
not a part: Fragment: a frequency adverb ('mostly 2 mm'), kept in RDF as a frequency, not a bearer.

not a part: A fragment of a comparison ('petiole 0.5-2 times blade length'): the bearer is the petiole (PO_0020038) and the ratio of its length to that of the leaf lamina is pattern 10, not an amount of a part.

not a part: A fragment of a comparison ('distal leaves 1-2.5 times head heights'): a length ratio of the described part to the capitulum (head is a BROAD synonym of capitulum inflorescence), pattern 10.
not a part: The abbreviation 'circa' (approximately), a qualifier on a value; it should be stripped by the value parser, not read as a part.

not a part: A karyological character of the organism (the somatic chromosome count, '2n = 84'), not a plant structure; PATO ploidy (PATO_0001374) is related but is not the count. The previous review rejected 'chromosome' likewise.
not a part: A shape quality (acuminate) misread as a part; the French 'acumen' (drip tip) is the leaf apex region, and the previous review rejected 'acumen' as a generic part without its organ.
not a part: A negated phrase: 'without' should be parsed as the quality absent and 'basal lobe' as the bearer. The leftover word is a fragment, not a structure.

A generic part that needs the organ it belongs to (trunk emergences, apical extensions, etc.), as 'appendage' was rejected. The prickle-bearing trunk bosses could later go to a stem emergence class if one is made.
Pores in the walls of Sphagnum hyaline cells. 'Pore' alone was rejected as generic, and its bearer (hyaline cell) has no class. Decide on a hyaline cell class first.
'Rib' was rejected as generic. Here the ribs probably belong to a moss capsule (8 long alternating with 8 short), but the organ is not in the examples.
Thin spots (pseudopores) in hyaline-cell walls of Sphagnum. A feature of a cell wall that needs its cell, and no hyaline cell class exists.
'Region' is a fragment ('region transversely triangular, opaque, in 3 rows'). It needs the leaf or cell type it belongs to.
not a part: A width given in numbers of cells ('lamina 25-30 cells across'), i.e. a measure of the described lamina, not a part. It should be read as a width with the unit 'cells'.
A generic word: membrane gaps in Sphagnum hyaline cells need the cell they belong to (no class).

'Pseudo' means it is not a true rhizome. The warty organ that is brown outside and red inside is probably the tuber-like body of a root parasite, so mapping it to rhizome (PO_0004542) is doubtful. The examples do not settle which organ it is.

Two different senses. 'Tentacules glanduligères' are Drosera's stalked glands, which are emergences rather than plain glandular trichomes (PO_0004509). 'Up to 8 inconspicuous tentacles' are appendages of some other organ. No single class fits.
not a part: Fragment of French '-sérié(es)' ('3-sérié', '10-13-sériées'), meaning arranged in n series. That is a quality word; the previous review rejected 'seriate' as not a structure.
French 'axe floral' means either the inflorescence axis (PO_0020122) or the receptacle (PO_0009064). Hooked, rusty and velvety axes suggest the first, but this cannot be decided without the taxon.
not a part: Fragment of French '-jugué(es)' (= -jugate, pairs of leaflets). It belongs in the counted-parts rule 'jugate -> leaflet, collection size 2'; add the French form 'jugué' there.
A general part ('languette', 'produced into a triangular tongue') that needs the organ it belongs to, like 'appendage' and 'lobule' in the previous review.
'Appendage' was rejected as a general part that needs its organ. 'Primary' only gives a rank in a series, and the organ is not stated.
Same as 'primary appendage': a general part with a rank, and no organ.
not a part: A row is an arrangement of glands, not a structure. The bearer is gland (PO_0005656), and the number of rows describes how the glands are arranged.
